gloss: to keep an eye on; to watch over attentively

definitions.gloss: to keep an eye out; to watch over a whole area attentively
definitions.explanation: To spread one's attention over several people, places, or details at once so that nothing is missed. Typical of teachers, staff, and anyone responsible for a group, and carries a sense of conscientious care rather than suspicion.

examples.japanese: {周|まわ}りに{目|め}を{配|くば}る。
examples.english: Keep an eye on your surroundings.

examples.japanese: {店長|てんちょう}は{店内|てんない}{全体|ぜんたい}に{目|め}を{配|くば}っている。
examples.english: The manager keeps an eye on the whole store.

examples.japanese: {担任|たんにん}は{一人一人|ひとりひとり}の{様子|ようす}に{目|め}を{配|くば}り、{小|ちい}さな{変化|へんか}も{見逃|みのが}さない。
examples.english: The homeroom teacher watches over each student closely and misses no small change.

notes:
USAGE:
The thing watched over takes に. Because {配|くば}る means "to distribute," the phrase implies attention spread across a whole scene, so the object is often a group or an area rather than a single item.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {周囲|しゅうい}に{目|め}を{配|くば}る: to keep an eye on one's surroundings
- {安全|あんぜん}に{目|め}を{配|くば}る: to watch out for safety
- {細|こま}かいところまで{目|め}を{配|くば}る: to attend to every detail

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {気|き}を{配|くば}る: to be considerate — attention to others' comfort, not visual watching
- {目|め}を{光|ひか}らせる: to keep a sharp watch — suspicious and policing in tone
